thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: routing-service #prod - increased 5xx rate from 0.2% -> 8% in eu-west-1, triggered at 2026-03-15T09:12:57Z. Paging maya (on-call).

maya (on-call): I’m on it. Can someone post quick customer impact? Is this API or streaming?

karen (prod-ops): API (text generation). Alerting telemetry shows errors primarily on routes that use model: redwood-large-v2 and some fallbacks to redwood-medium. ~12% of requests are falling back and then 5xxing.

sri: Initial hypothesis: regional spillover + fallback mismatch. eu-west autoscaler hit a limit at 09:09, routing started spilling to us-west but still tagging requests as eu region which confused a model-compat check -> 422/500 cascade.

joel: I can confirm autoscaler logs show multiple PGs at 100% GPU mem and long queue times. Pushing list of relevant logs here: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1779999999/autoscaler.log (short link: https://logs.redwood/internal/1779999999)

maya (on-call): Thanks. Can someone run a quick query for error signatures and correlation IDs? I want an example request that failed so we can trace.

drew (sre): Running: 
```
query errors where service="routing-service" and region="eu-west-1" | sort desc | limit 200
```
Found many entries with error="ModelVariantMismatchError" and a few with "KVCacheMiss" just before 5xx.

sri: That matches. The routing fallback policy probably tried to map to a quantized variant that isn't compatible with the large model signature when spillover happens.

joel: Pasting a representative log snippet (redacted):
```
[09:10:33Z] req_id=abcd1234 route=/v1/completions region=eu-west-1 routed_to=us-west-2 model=redwood-medium-quant error=ModelVariantMismatchError: tokenizer-vocab-mismatch
```

maya (on-call): Customer impact: two enterprise tenants in EU experienced elevated latency and some errors (support ticket opened). Karen, can you annotate which customers?

karen (prod-ops): Ticket IDs: #38412 (ACME EMEA), #38418 (FinData). Both reported 502s and slow tails during 09:10-09:24 UTC.

maya (on-call): Okay mitigation plan — short term: disable cross-region spillover for eu-west-1 and force local degrade policy to fallback to redwood-medium-compat (non-quant) while we stabilize. Who can flip the routing flag?

drew (sre): I can. Will push a temporary policy change: set routing-policy.eu-west-1.spillover = false and routing-policy.eu-west-1.fallback = redwood-medium-compat. Executing now.

deploy-bot: deploy started by drew — changelist 5247 — routing-config-service — set spillover=false for eu-west-1

drew (sre): Done. Confirmed routes now return 200 hits for the new fallback policy. Monitoring.

sam: Running a smoke loop against both ACME and FinData tenants to validate: 
```
for id in ACME FinData; do curl -sS -H "X-Customer-ID:$id" https://api.redwood/v1/generate | jq .status; done
```
Both got 200s on retry.

maya (on-call): Good. Keep an eye on latency tail. We should capture a timeline and hypotheses to include in the RCA. I'll start a high-level timeline in the thread. Everyone drop corroborating logs and commands.

maya (on-call): Timeline (initial):
- 09:08 UTC: eu-west-1 GPU pool begins hitting mem pressure
- 09:09 UTC: autoscaler scales, but spike exceeds quick scale headroom
- 09:10 UTC: routing-service starts spillover to other regions (policy) — some requests map to quantized variants
- 09:10-09:24 UTC: increased ModelVariantMismatchError and 5xx -> customer impact
- 09:17 UTC: page on-call
- 09:22 UTC: routing-policy override pushed (spillover disabled, forced compat fallback)
- 09:25 UTC: errors drop, recovery in progress

joel: Adding logs for the autoscaler decision matrix: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1779999999/autoscaler-decisions.json

sri: Hypotheses:
1) Fallback selection logic didn't validate tokenizer/model signature before routing (model-compat check deferred).
2) KV cache eviction during spillover introduced transient cache misses that surfaced as mismatches in downstream model loading.
3) Autoscaler config allowed too-aggressive spillover when local burst headroom exists but capacity is fragmented.

karen (prod-ops): Note: tenant ACME was using a pinned version redwood-large-v2@2026-02-10 which does not have a quantized equivalent; fallback should have respected pinning but apparently fell back to quantized medium.

maya (on-call): Action items during incident (short-term):
- drew: run full config audit for fallback mapping rules (due ASAP)
- sri: validate model-compat checks and add pre-routing validation (postmortem/PR)
- joel: collect a bundle of routing logs + sample requests with req_id -> put into incident S3
- karen: notify ACME and FinData with status and mitigation steps (done)

drew (sre): Starting config audit. Quick check shows a missing explicit rule for pinned-version handling in spillover codepath. Opening ticket: #INC-5421.

joel: Uploading bundle: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1779999999/bundle.tar.gz (sha256: c3f2...) — includes traces, routing decisions, model-variant table.

maya (on-call): Forensics: attach a few correlation IDs here so research can trace full path. req_ids: abcd1234, efgh5678, ijkl9012.

sri: I pulled abcd1234 trace — route: eu-west-1 -> router selected redwood-medium-quant due to policy order. There is a preflight check that should have rejected quantized model for redwood-large-v2 requests but it only runs post-routing in this codepath.

karen (prod-ops): Customers updated. Support will follow up with logs. No SLA breaches yet but we'll track.

maya (on-call): Closing mitigation: monitoring window until 10:00 UTC. If stable, we'll demote this to an RCA thread. Thanks team. Please keep posting any missing logs or odd artifacts.

sri: Quick mitigation note for RCA: we should add a sanity check in routing-policy that verifies tokenizer/model_signature compatibility before any cross-region reassign.

drew (sre): Also recommend a short-term rule: prioritize local degrade/hot-requeue instead of immediate spillover when pinned versions exist. I'll add to INC-5421.

joel: One more thing I noticed: a small subset of requests had KVCacheMiss followed immediately by ModelLoadLatency > 1.2s — could be startup cost for a variant that wasn't prewarmed during spillover.

maya (on-call): Nice catch. Add prewarm policy to the list (postmortem/mitigation): prewarm fallback variants when spillover is enabled.

deploy-bot: after_action: routing-config-service - rolled back spillover change at 09:58 UTC for testing. (Note: final policy change pending RCA)

maya (on-call): Thanks everyone. I'll start drafting RCA with timeline, hypotheses, logs, and recommended fixes. Tag me for review. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity: Sev2. Incident ID: INC-1779999999.
